citation.title: Stress-constrained optimization of multiscale structures with parameterized microarchitectures using machine learning

claim.primary_outcome_paraphrase: Neural surrogates predict local stress 1,000–10,000 times faster than full-scale evaluation or successive homogenization, with reported stress predictions within 10–15% of ground truth.
claim.claimed_speedup_basis: Section 3 reports evaluation speedups of 1,000–10,000 times; the numeric field stores the lower end of that reported range.
claim.alternatives: Abstract and Section 6 report that the multiscale designs do not outperform density-based topology optimization in stress-constrained volume minimization; in a multifunctional example they use more material but better match target displacement (Section 5.3).

baseline.classical_method: Full-scale finite-element evaluation or successive unit-cell homogenization for local stress evaluation; density-based topology optimization is also used for design-quality comparisons
baseline.solver: Finite-element analysis and homogenization; linear solver not stated
baseline.problem_size: Four pedagogical local-stress cases; optimization examples include domains discretized into 5,632 and 5,000 microstructures (Section 5.2)
baseline.classical_time: not stated; evaluation speedup reported as 1,000–10,000 times
baseline.ml_time: not stated; evaluation speedup reported as 1,000–10,000 times
baseline.data_generation_cost: Approximately one hour to generate training data on Intel i7 at 4.1 GHz, 4 cores; Section 3 reports 1,000 examples for constitutive tensors and 10,000 for stress amplification
baseline.quality_metric: Relative error norm / RRMSE for maximum microstructural von Mises stress; stress-constraint violation and volume fraction in optimized designs
baseline.quality_gap: Predicted maximum stress is within 10–15% of ground truth (Section 3); optimized multiscale designs have 1–2% stress-constraint violation in the reported examples (Section 5.2).

R1.evidence: Section 3: the surrogate evaluations are compared with full-scale FE/homogenization and reported within 10–15% of ground truth, alongside the speedup claim.

R2.evidence: Sections 3 and 5: the text names full-scale FE and successive homogenization comparators but does not establish an inefficient solver, hardware mismatch, or fixed-iteration excess.

R3.evidence: Section 3 reports data generation of about one hour and training-set sizes, but not neural-network training time or break-even use count; Section 6 notes data-generation time should be considered.

R4.evidence: Sections 4–5 use surrogate-predicted stresses within optimization and report example constraint violations; the returned optimized designs are not reported as FE-verified.

reporting.n_test_cases: Four pedagogical local-stress test cases (Section 3); multiple optimization examples including L-bracket, double L-bracket, stress-concentration, and multifunctional designs (Sections 5.1–5.3).

notes: Full text accessed as open-access version of record. The 1,000–10,000× claim concerns local stress evaluations inside the design workflow, not a timed end-to-end optimization comparison.
